title: 금요일 밤 포차, 뒷담화와 짝사랑
title_en: Friday night at the pojangmacha: gossip and a crush
summary: 대학 동기 지수와 현우가 포차에서 꼰대 팀장과 얌체 동기 뒷담화를 하다가, 현우의 짝사랑 이야기에 빠져 막차 시간까지 잊어버리는 이야기.

items.gloss: in case…, for fear that… (as a short answer)
items.meaning: (I'm doing this) in case / for fear that...
items.example: 왜 안 자냐고? 내일 발표 망칠까 봐.
items.translation: Why am I still up? I'm just scared I'll mess up my presentation tomorrow.
items.note: In casual talk the second half (걱정돼서 그래) is dropped, so -ㄹ까 봐 ends the sentence as a reason. / 왜 이렇게 일찍 왔어? 늦을까 봐. = Why so early? In case I was late.

items.gloss: (someone) did A, and then B (something you saw)
items.meaning: (someone) did A, and then B happened (something you saw)
items.example: 미카가 아까 전화 받더니 갑자기 뛰어나가더라. 무슨 일 있나?
items.translation: Mika took a call earlier and suddenly ran out. Is something up?
items.note: vs -았/었더니: -았/었더니 is for your own action and its result; -더니 reports what you saw someone else do. / Same subject in both halves, and not 'I'. / 밥 먹더니 바로 자더라 = ate and went straight to sleep

items.meaning: Realisation, 반말 / self-talk form of -군요
items.example: 너 이 영화 벌써 봤구나? 스포 하지 마!
items.translation: Oh, you've already seen this movie? No spoilers!
items.note: Verb + 는구나 (먹는구나) · adjective + 구나 (춥구나) · past 았/었구나 (아팠구나) / For friends, younger people, or muttering to yourself. Never to seniors: use -군요/-네요.

items.meaning: Ah, so that's why... (반말)
items.example: 감기 걸렸었어? 그래서 어제 연락이 없었구나.
items.translation: You had a cold? So that's why I didn't hear from you yesterday.
items.note: Polite: 아, 그래서 안 오셨군요 / 열이 나다 = to have a fever · 결석하다 = to be absent · -느라고 = because I was busy doing

items.meaning: "I thought (wrongly) that..."
items.example: 두 분이 같이 오신 줄 알았어요. 따로 오셨어요?
items.translation: I thought you two came together. Did you come separately?
items.note: vs -은/는 줄 몰랐어요: 사귀는 줄 알았어 = I thought they were dating (they aren't); 사귀는 줄 몰랐어 = I didn't know they were dating (they are). / Same conjugation as -은/는 줄 몰랐어요.

items.meaning: To go around together, to hang out together
items.example: 두 분 항상 같이 다니셔서 사귀는 줄 알았어요.
items.translation: You two are always together, so I thought you were dating.
items.note: 붙어 다니다 = be inseparable · 어디를 가도 = wherever (they) go / -아/어 다니다 = go around doing: 들고 다니다 = carry around

items.gloss: six of one, half a dozen of the other
items.meaning: There's little to choose between them. Lit. "Measuring the height of acorns."
items.example: 둘 다 거기서 거기야. 완전 도토리 키 재기지.
items.translation: They're both about the same. Six of one, half a dozen of the other.
items.note: Slightly dismissive: the options are all equally average. / 키를 재다 = measure height · 비슷비슷하다 = all about the same / Noun phrase, takes 이다.

items.meaning: "I hear that..., so..."
items.example: 주말에 날씨 완전 좋다는데, 한강 갈래?
items.translation: They say the weather's going to be great this weekend. Want to go to the Han River?
items.note: Adjective → -다는데: 화창하다는데, 춥다는데 / 화창하다 = bright and sunny · 산책(을) 나가다 = go out for a walk

items.meaning: "so... that...": stressing how intense something is
items.example: 거기 김치찌개가 얼마나 맛있는지, 맨날 줄 서야 돼요.
items.translation: That place's kimchi jjigae is so good you always have to queue.
items.note: Verb -는지 · adjective -(으)ㄴ지 · noun -인지 · past -았/었는지 / Action verbs need a degree adverb: 얼마나 잘하는지 (not 얼마나 하는지). Emotion verbs don't: 얼마나 좋아하는지

items.meaning: What do you mean, no? (flatly contradicting a denial)
items.example: 아니긴 뭐가 아니야, 얼굴이 반쪽인데.
items.translation: What do you mean you're not? You look totally drained.
items.note: A-긴 뭐가 A야 = what do you mean A: 괜찮긴 뭐가 괜찮아 = you're not okay at all / 얼굴이 반쪽이 되다 = look gaunt, worn out / 반말 only, between close friends or family.

items.gloss: are you out of your mind?
items.meaning: Are you out of your mind?
items.example: 새벽 3시에 혼자 등산을 간다고? 너 제정신이니?
items.translation: You're going hiking alone at 3am? Are you out of your mind?
items.note: Strong; only with close friends or when genuinely shocked. Lighter: 너 미쳤어? / 제정신이 아니다 = not in one's right mind · 정신 차려 = get a grip

items.gloss: to be cheeky and selfish, a freeloader
items.meaning: to be cheeky and selfish, a freeloader
items.example: 맨날 계산할 때만 화장실 가더라. 완전 얌체 같아.
items.translation: They always go to the bathroom right when it's time to pay. Such a freeloader.
items.note: 얌체 = someone who takes advantage without shame (cutting in line, never paying their share). / 얌체 짓 = a cheeky, selfish move · 얌체 운전 = cutting in on the road

items.meaning: rather, might as well (the lesser of two evils)
items.example: 이 시간엔 버스 완전 막혀. 차라리 걸어가는 게 빠르겠다.
items.translation: The buses are jammed at this hour. It'd be quicker to just walk.
items.note: vs 오히려: 오히려 = on the contrary, unexpectedly (오히려 더 좋아); 차라리 = 'I'd rather', picking the less bad option. / 차라리 잘됐다 = it's actually for the best · 차라리 안 하는 게 낫다 = better not to do it at all

items.meaning: should have just…
items.example: 이렇게 막힐 거면 차라리 지하철 탈 걸, 아 진짜.
items.translation: If it was going to be this jammed, I should've just taken the subway. Ugh, seriously.
items.note: 차라리 -(으)ㄹ 걸 (그랬다) = should have just… / 차라리 -는 게 낫다 = I'd rather

items.meaning: secretly, behind someone's back
items.example: 동생 몰래 간식 꺼내 먹었는데, 들킬 것 같아.
items.translation: I ate the snacks without my sibling knowing, and I think I'm about to get caught.
items.note: N 몰래 = without N knowing. / 엄마 몰래 = behind Mom's back · 몰래 나가다 = sneak out · 몰래카메라 (몰카) = hidden camera

items.gloss: don't talk about what you don't know
items.meaning: Don't talk about what you don't know.
items.example: 모르는 소리 좀 하지 마. 해 보면 진짜 장난 아니야.
items.translation: You don't know what you're talking about. Try it and it's no joke.
items.note: 반말 and fairly blunt; only with close friends. 소리 here = talk, remarks. / 무슨 소리야 = what are you talking about · 말도 안 되는 소리 = nonsense

items.meaning: What are you talking about?
items.example: 무슨 소리야? 나 그런 말 한 적 없거든?
items.translation: What are you talking about? I never said that.
items.note: 반말; polite form is 무슨 소리예요? / Also brushes off thanks or apologies: 무슨 소리야, 당연히 도와줘야지 = don't be silly, of course I'll help

items.gloss: why do you keep changing your mind?
items.meaning: Why do you keep changing your mind?
items.example: 아까는 좋다며. 왜 이랬다 저랬다 해?
items.translation: You said you liked it earlier. Why do you keep changing your mind?
items.note: 반말; with friends or family. / -았다 -었다 하다 = keep switching between two things: 왔다 갔다 하다 = go back and forth · 껐다 켰다 하다 = flick on and off

items.meaning: To agree with what someone says; to chime in
items.example: 제 친구는 맞장구를 잘 쳐 줘서 얘기할 맛이 나요.
items.translation: My friend is great at chiming in, so talking to them is fun.
items.note: Typical 맞장구: 진짜요? · 그러니까요 = I know, right? · 맞아요 · 대박 / Always with 치다; also written 맞장구치다.

items.meaning: secret
items.example: 이거 진짜 비밀이야. 아무한테도 말하면 안 돼.
items.translation: This is a real secret. You can't tell anyone.
items.note: 비밀을 지키다 = keep a secret · 비밀을 털어놓다 = confide a secret · 비밀번호 = password

items.meaning: repeatedly, keep (doing something)
items.example: 그 사람 얼굴이 자꾸 생각나. 나 왜 이래?
items.translation: I keep thinking about that person's face. What's wrong with me?
items.note: vs 계속: 계속 is neutral 'continuously'; 자꾸 is 'again and again', often annoying or out of your control. / 자꾸 왜 그래? = why do you keep doing that? · 자꾸 까먹어 = I keep forgetting

items.meaning: to have a distinctive voice
items.example: 이 가수 목소리 진짜 독특하죠? 한 번 들으면 안 잊혀요.
items.translation: This singer's voice is really distinctive, right? Hear it once and you can't forget it.
items.note: vs 특이하다: 특이하다 is 'unusual, odd' and can sound negative; 독특하다 is 'distinctive', usually a compliment. / 목소리가 좋다 = have a nice voice · 독특한 스타일 = a distinctive style

items.gloss: this and that, all sorts of
items.meaning: various, all sorts of
items.example: 어제 걔랑 이런저런 얘기 하다 보니까 새벽이더라.
items.translation: I was chatting with them about this and that yesterday, and suddenly it was the middle of the night.
items.note: 이런저런 얘기 = this and that · 이런저런 이유로 = for various reasons / Similar: 이것저것 = this and that (things) · 여기저기 = here and there

items.meaning: to tap, to give a light knock (e.g. on the shoulder)
items.example: 누가 뒤에서 어깨를 툭 치길래 봤더니 너였어?
items.translation: Someone tapped me on the shoulder from behind, and it was you?
items.note: 툭 = a light, sudden tap or drop: 툭 떨어지다 = drop with a plop · 툭하면 = at the drop of a hat (툭하면 화내) / 어깨를 치다 = tap someone's shoulder

items.meaning: to swear; to badmouth, speak ill of
items.example: 뒤에서 남 욕하는 사람은 좀 별로더라.
items.translation: I'm just not into people who badmouth others behind their backs.
items.note: Two senses: swear (욕을 하다) and badmouth someone (남을 욕하다). / 욕을 먹다 = get criticised · 뒷담화 = gossip behind someone's back (casual)

items.meaning: To be flustered, to be taken aback
items.example: 교수님이 갑자기 제 이름 부르셔서 좀 당황했어요.
items.translation: The professor suddenly called my name, so I got a bit flustered.
items.note: vs 황당하다: 당황하다 is you being flustered; 황당하다 is the situation being absurd (황당한 일이 있었어). / 당황스럽다 = disconcerting · 당황하지 마세요 = don't panic

items.meaning: To be relatable
items.example: 그 노래 가사가 너무 공감돼서 계속 듣게 돼요.
items.translation: The lyrics of that song are so relatable, I keep listening to it.
items.note: vs 공감하다: 공감되다 describes the thing (이 노래 너무 공감돼); 공감하다 is the person (네 말에 공감해). / 공감(이) 가다 = relatable · 공감 능력 = empathy

items.meaning: To laugh, to break into a smile
items.example: 그 얘기 생각하면 아직도 웃음이 나요.
items.translation: I still laugh whenever I think about that story.
items.note: vs 웃다: 웃음이 나다 is laughter coming out on its own, often when you shouldn't. / 웃음이 터지다 = burst out laughing · 웃음을 참다 = hold back a laugh / Same 나다 as 열이 나다, 화가 나다.

items.gloss: to take it out on someone
items.meaning: To vent one's anger, to take it out on someone
items.example: 회사에서 짜증 난 걸 왜 저한테 화풀이해요?
items.translation: Why are you taking your work frustrations out on me?
items.note: vs 짜증 내다: 짜증 내다 is being snappy in general; 화풀이하다 is taking anger out on someone who didn't cause it. / N한테 화풀이하다 = take it out on N · 애꿎은 사람한테 화풀이 = venting on an innocent person

items.gloss: to ignore; to look down on
items.meaning: To ignore, to disregard, to look down on
items.example: 내 말은 맨날 무시하고… 진짜 서운해.
items.translation: You always ignore what I say... it really hurts.
items.note: Two senses: ignore (전화를 무시하다) and look down on (사람을 무시하다). Context decides. / 무시당하다 = be ignored or looked down on · 나 무시해? = are you looking down on me?

items.meaning: To not be able to get through to someone
items.example: 그 사람이랑은 진짜 얘기가 안 통해요. 답답해 죽겠어요.
items.translation: I just can't get through to that person. It's driving me crazy.
items.note: 말이 안 통하다 = can't communicate (also a language barrier) · 말이 잘 통하다 = really click with someone · 얘기가 통하는 사람 = someone you can talk to

items.meaning: An actress
items.example: 그 여배우 이번에 상 받았대. 드디어!
items.translation: That actress won an award this time. Finally!
items.note: 배우 alone is gender-neutral and usually preferred these days. / 상을 받다 = win an award · 주연 배우 = lead actor · 조연 = supporting role

items.meaning: To be cruel, brutal, gory
items.example: 그 영화 너무 잔인해서 중간에 눈 감았어요.
items.translation: That movie was so brutal I closed my eyes halfway through.
items.note: 잔인한 장면 = gory or violent scene · 너 진짜 잔인하다 = you're so cruel (often teasing)

items.meaning: To get the chills, to be spine-chilling
items.example: 그 장면 진짜 오싹하지 않았어? 소름 돋았어.
items.translation: Wasn't that scene seriously creepy? I got goosebumps.
items.note: vs 으스스하다: both mean creepy; 으스스하다 leans more to a spooky place or shivery cold. / 등골이 오싹하다 = a chill runs down your spine · 오싹한 이야기 = a creepy story

items.meaning: To stay up all night
items.example: 과제 때문에 이틀이나 밤새웠어… 죽겠다.
items.translation: I pulled two all-nighters for this assignment… I'm dying.
items.note: vs 밤새다: 밤새다 is the night passing (밤새 비가 왔어요); staying up is 밤새우다. People mix them up in speech. / 밤을 새우다 = same thing · 밤샘 = an all-nighter

items.gloss: drinking snacks; something to chew over with drinks
items.meaning: Snacks eaten with alcohol; also something to reminisce about over drinks
items.example: 안줏거리 뭐 시킬까? 골뱅이 어때?
items.translation: What should we order to go with the drinks? How about spicy whelk?
items.note: 안주 + -거리 (material for). Also figurative: an old story retold over drinks. / 술안주 = drinking food · 이야깃거리 = something to talk about

items.meaning: To be stubborn, to be headstrong
items.example: 우리 아빠 고집이 진짜 세. 한번 정하면 끝이야.
items.translation: My dad is so stubborn. Once he's decided, that's it.
items.note: 세다 here = strong, not count. / 고집을 부리다 = dig your heels in · 고집쟁이 = a stubborn person

items.meaning: At one time, at one point
items.example: 나도 한때 그 노래 진짜 많이 들었는데. 추억이다.
items.translation: There was a time I listened to that song a ton too. Brings back memories.
items.note: 한때 유행했다 = was trendy for a while · 한때는 = there was a time when / Weather reports: 한때 비 = rain at times

items.meaning: The last train or bus of the night
items.example: 막차 놓쳤다… 택시비 또 나가네.
items.translation: Missed the last train… there goes more money on a taxi.
items.note: Opposite: 첫차 = first train/bus · 막차 끊기다 = the last train has gone (막차 끊겼어) / 막- = last: 막내 = youngest

items.meaning: to be typical, classic (of a type)
items.example: 양말에 샌들이라니… 완전 전형적인 한국 아빠 패션이다.
items.translation: Socks with sandals... that's a textbook Korean dad look.
items.note: 전형적인 N = a classic/textbook N (전형적인 직장인 = a typical office worker) · 뻔하다 = predictable, the more casual word for a cliché plot

ov.blurb: Over whelks and soju, Jisu vents about her boss and grills Hyunwoo about his crush.
ov.overview: Jisu and Hyunwoo are university friends meeting at a street-tent bar on a Friday night. Jisu vents about a stubborn team leader who passed off her idea as his own, and they moan about Minji, a classmate who always disappears when the bill comes. Then Jisu teases out Hyunwoo's crush on Daeun, the vocalist in his band club, whom he plans to confess to after next week's show. Daeun texts asking him to a horror film, the genre he's terrified of, and the pair miss the last train.
ov.setting: Pojangmacha on a Friday night, two university friends
ov.register: 반말 between friends throughout, 해요체 only when ordering from the owner

lines.ko: 현우야! 여기, 여기!
lines.en: Hyunwoo! Over here, here!

lines.ko: 야, 정지수. 너 왜 이렇게 일찍 왔어?
lines.en: Hey, Jung Jisu. Why are you here so early?

lines.ko: 늦을까 봐. 너 저번에 나 십 분 늦었다고 한 시간 내내 뭐라 했잖아.
lines.en: In case I was late. Last time I was ten minutes late, you nagged me for a whole hour.

lines.ko: 기억력 좋네. 뭐 시켰어?
lines.en: Good memory. What'd you order?

lines.ko: 아직. 안줏거리 뭐 할까? 골뱅이 어때?
lines.en: Nothing yet. What should we get to snack on? Whelks?

lines.ko: 좋지. 계란말이도 하자.
lines.en: Sure. Let's get a rolled omelette too.

lines.ko: 사장님! 여기 골뱅이무침이랑 계란말이 하나요! 소주도 한 병 주세요!
lines.en: Excuse me! One spicy whelk salad and a rolled omelette, please! And a bottle of soju!

lines.ko: 근데 너 얼굴이 왜 그래? 완전 반쪽 됐네.
lines.en: But what's with your face? You look totally wiped out.

lines.ko: 아, 오늘 진짜 최악이었어. 우리 팀장 있잖아.
lines.en: Ugh, today was the absolute worst. You know my team leader.

lines.ko: 또? 그 고집 센 팀장?
lines.en: Again? The stubborn one?

lines.ko: 응. 아침에 부장님한테 엄청 깨지더니, 자리 오자마자 나한테 화풀이하더라.
lines.en: Yep. He got chewed out by the department head this morning, and the second he got back to his desk he took it out on me.

lines.ko: 뭐? 너한테 왜?
lines.en: What? Why you?

lines.ko: 몰라. 내 보고서에 오타 하나 있다고, 사무실 사람들 다 들리게 소리를 지르는 거야. 나 진짜 당황했어.
lines.en: No idea. Because there was one typo in my report, he yelled so the whole office could hear. I was so thrown.

lines.ko: 와, 너무했다.
lines.en: Wow, that's way out of line.

lines.ko: 더 웃긴 게 뭔지 알아? 지난주엔 내 아이디어를 그렇게 무시하더니, 오늘 회의에서 자기 아이디어인 것처럼 발표하는 거 있지.
lines.en: You know what's even better? Last week he brushed off my idea, and today in the meeting he presented it like it was his own.

lines.ko: 헐. 완전 전형적인 꼰대네.
lines.en: Wow. Classic old-school jerk boss.

lines.ko: 그치? 고집이 얼마나 센지, 한번 정하면 아무도 못 말려. 진짜 얘기가 안 통해.
lines.en: Right? He's so stubborn that once he's decided something, no one can stop him. You just can't get through to him.

lines.ko: 그럼 차라리 부장님한테 말해.
lines.en: Then just go to the department head instead.

lines.ko: 모르는 소리 좀 하지 마. 부장님이랑 팀장, 같은 대학 선후배야.
lines.en: You don't know what you're talking about. The department head and my team leader went to the same university, senior and junior.

lines.ko: 아, 진짜?
lines.en: Oh, seriously?

lines.ko: 응. 말해 봤자 나만 이상한 사람 돼.
lines.en: Yeah. Even if I said something, I'd be the one who looks weird.

lines.ko: 아… 그래서 너 요즘 연락이 없었구나.
lines.en: Ah… so that's why I haven't heard from you lately.

lines.ko: 응, 정신이 하나도 없었어.
lines.en: Yeah, I've been all over the place.

lines.ko: 근데 그런 사람은 어디에나 있나 봐. 우리 팀에도 김 대리 있잖아.
lines.en: Guess people like that are everywhere. We've got Assistant Manager Kim on my team, remember?

lines.ko: 아, 맨날 커피 사 온다는 그 사람?
lines.en: Oh, the guy who always brings coffee?

lines.ko: 응. 커피는 사 오는데 일은 하나도 안 해. 지난주엔 내가 밤새 만든 자료를, 부장님 앞에서 자기가 발표하더라.
lines.en: Yep. He brings coffee, but does zero work. Last week he presented the material I stayed up all night making, right in front of the department head.

lines.ko: 헐, 똑같네. 그래서 넌 가만히 있었어?
lines.en: No way, same thing. So you just let it go?

lines.ko: 어떡해, 선배인데. 그냥 웃었지. 대신 이제 자료는 내가 부장님한테 직접 메일로 보내.
lines.en: What can I do, he's my senior. I just smiled. But now I email my stuff straight to the department head.

lines.ko: 오, 똑똑하네. 아, 맞다. 너 민지 얘기 들었어?
lines.en: Ooh, smart. Oh, right. Did you hear about Minji?

lines.ko: 민지? 우리 동기 민지?
lines.en: Minji? Our classmate Minji?

lines.ko: 응. 지난주에 동기 모임 했잖아, 너 야근해서 못 왔을 때. 걔 또 계산할 때 화장실 갔다?
lines.en: Yeah. We had that class get-together last week, when you couldn't come because of overtime. She went to the bathroom right when the bill came. Again.

lines.ko: 또? 걔 맨날 그러잖아.
lines.en: Again? She always does that.

lines.ko: 그니까. 근데 이번엔 화장실 간다고 하더니 몰래 집에 가 버렸어.
lines.en: I know. But this time she said she was going to the bathroom and then snuck off home.

lines.ko: 헐, 진짜 얌체 같다.
lines.en: Wow, what a freeloader.

lines.ko: 그치? 그리고 이건 진짜 비밀인데… 아무한테도 말하면 안 돼.
lines.en: Right? And this is a real secret… you can't tell anyone.

lines.ko: 뭔데? 나 입 무거운 거 알잖아.
lines.en: What is it? You know I can keep my mouth shut.

lines.ko: 민지가 다른 애들한테 내 욕하고 다닌대. 내가 맨날 회사 얘기만 해서 지루하다고.
lines.en: Apparently Minji's been badmouthing me to everyone. Saying I'm boring because all I talk about is work.

lines.ko: 뭐? 웃기네. 자기가 제일 회사 얘기 많이 하면서.
lines.en: What? That's rich. She talks about work more than anyone.

lines.ko: 내 말이! 와, 넌 맞장구를 진짜 잘 쳐 줘서 얘기할 맛이 난다.
lines.en: Exactly! Wow, you're so good at backing me up, it actually makes me want to talk.

lines.ko: 진심이야. 그래서 넌 뭐라고 했어?
lines.en: I mean it. So what did you say?

lines.ko: 아무 말도 안 했지. 그냥 웃었어. 근데 생각할수록 열받아.
lines.en: Nothing. I just laughed. But the more I think about it, the angrier I get.

lines.ko: 열받을 만하지.
lines.en: You've got every right to be.

lines.ko: 아, 됐어. 오늘은 그만 욕하자. 네 얘기나 해 봐. 너 요즘 밴드 동호회 열심히 나간다며?
lines.en: Ugh, forget it. Enough trashing people tonight. Tell me about you. I hear you've been going to your band club a lot lately?

lines.ko: 어? 응, 그냥 뭐.
lines.en: Huh? Yeah, I guess.

lines.ko: 거기 보컬 하는 애, 다은이? 너네 요즘 맨날 같이 다니던데.
lines.en: That vocalist, Daeun? You two are always together these days.

lines.ko: 같이 다니긴 뭘 같이 다녀. 연습 끝나고 집 방향이 같아서 같이 가는 거야.
lines.en: Together, my foot. We just head the same way home after practice.

lines.ko: 난 너네 사귀는 줄 알았어.
lines.en: I thought you two were dating.

lines.ko: 무슨 소리야. 우리 그냥 친구야.
lines.en: What are you talking about? We're just friends.

lines.ko: 그래? 근데 얼굴은 왜 빨개져?
lines.en: Oh yeah? Then why's your face going red?

lines.ko: 술 때문이지.
lines.en: It's the alcohol.

lines.ko: 아직 한 잔도 안 마셨거든?
lines.en: We haven't even had one glass yet.

lines.ko: 아… 아니야, 진짜 아무 사이 아니야.
lines.en: Uh… no, seriously, there's nothing going on.

lines.ko: 아니긴 뭐가 아니야. 귀까지 빨간데.
lines.en: What do you mean, no? Even your ears are red.

lines.ko: 아 알았어, 알았어. 사실… 좀 좋아해.
lines.en: Okay, okay. Actually… I kind of like her.

lines.ko: 대박! 너 진짜 다은이 좋아하는구나!
lines.en: No way! So you really do like Daeun!

lines.ko: 쉿, 조용히 해. 옆 테이블 다 듣겠다.
lines.en: Shh, keep it down. The next table will hear everything.

lines.ko: 언제부터? 빨리 말해 봐.
lines.en: Since when? Spill it.

lines.ko: 한 달 전쯤? 처음엔 그냥 노래 잘하는 애였는데… 목소리가 좀 독특하거든.
lines.en: About a month ago? At first she was just someone who sings well… but her voice is kind of unique.

lines.ko: 독특해? 어떻게?
lines.en: Unique how?

lines.ko: 몰라, 한 번 들으면 안 잊혀. 그 뒤로 자꾸 생각나.
lines.en: I don't know, once you hear it, you don't forget it. Ever since, I keep thinking about her.

lines.ko: 너 저번에 다은이 어떤 여배우 닮았다고 하지 않았어?
lines.en: Didn't you say Daeun looks like some actress?

lines.ko: 응, 그 여배우 있잖아. 이번에 상 받은. 웃을 때 좀 닮았어.
lines.en: Yeah, you know that actress. The one who just won an award. She looks a bit like her when she smiles.

lines.ko: 뭐야, 완전 빠졌네. 그래서, 무슨 일 있었는데?
lines.en: Oh my god, you've totally fallen for her. So what happened?

lines.ko: 지난주에 연습 끝나고, 둘이 편의점 앞에서 이런저런 얘기 하다 보니까 열두 시가 넘은 거야.
lines.en: Last week after practice, we got talking about this and that outside the convenience store, and suddenly it was past midnight.

lines.ko: 오, 좋은데?
lines.en: Ooh, nice.

lines.ko: 근데 헤어질 때 다은이가 내 어깨를 툭 치더니, "오늘 좀 멋있었어." 이러더라.
lines.en: And when we said bye, she gave my shoulder a little tap and went, "You were kind of cool today."

lines.ko: 헐, 그거 완전 그린라이트잖아!
lines.en: Oh my god, that's totally a green light!

lines.ko: 그치? 나도 그 생각만 하면 아직도 웃음이 나.
lines.en: Right? I still can't help grinning whenever I think about it.

lines.ko: 그래서 고백은 언제 할 건데?
lines.en: So when are you confessing?

lines.ko: 다음 주 공연 끝나고 하려고.
lines.en: After the show next week.

lines.ko: 오, 멋있다!
lines.en: Ooh, look at you!

lines.ko: 근데… 아니야, 그냥 하지 말까? 괜히 어색해질까 봐.
lines.en: But… no, maybe I shouldn't. I'm scared it'll just get awkward.

lines.ko: 아까는 한다며. 왜 이랬다 저랬다 해?
lines.en: You just said you would. Why do you keep changing your mind?

lines.ko: 아니, 고백했는데 차이면 동호회도 못 나가잖아.
lines.en: I mean, if I confess and get turned down, I can't even go to the club anymore.

lines.ko: 야, 그럴 거면 차라리 빨리 말해. 혼자 끙끙 앓는 것보다 훨씬 나아.
lines.en: Hey, if that's how it is, you might as well tell her soon. It's way better than suffering alone.

lines.ko: 말이 쉽지. 아, 그리고 다은이가 공포 영화를 엄청 좋아한다는데, 나 공포 영화 하나도 못 보잖아.
lines.en: Easy for you to say. Oh, and apparently Daeun loves horror movies, and you know I can't watch them at all.

lines.ko: 어, 알지.
lines.en: Yeah, I know.

lines.ko: 그래서 얘기라도 좀 하려고 어제 세 편 연달아 봤어. 밤새웠어.
lines.en: So I watched three in a row last night, just so I'd have something to talk about. Stayed up all night.

lines.ko: 제정신이니? 너 공포 영화 보면 화장실도 혼자 못 가잖아.
lines.en: Are you out of your mind? You can't even go to the bathroom alone after a horror movie.

lines.ko: 그니까. 첫 번째 건 너무 잔인해서 중간에 눈 감았고, 두 번째 건 마지막 장면이 너무 오싹해서 소름 돋았어.
lines.en: I know. The first one was so gory I shut my eyes halfway through, and the ending of the second one was so creepy I got goosebumps.

lines.ko: 아, 그래서 아까부터 하품했구나.
lines.en: Ah, so that's why you've been yawning this whole time.

lines.ko: 응. 근데 웃긴 게, 세 번째 영화에 주인공이 짝사랑하는 얘기가 나오는데… 그게 너무 공감돼서 혼자 울 뻔했어.
lines.en: Yeah. But the funny thing is, in the third movie the main character has this crush… and it was so relatable I nearly cried on my own.

lines.ko: 공포 영화 보면서? 너 진짜 중증이다.
lines.en: During a horror movie? You've got it bad.

lines.ko: 놀리지 마. 나 진지해.
lines.en: Don't make fun of me. I'm serious.

lines.ko: 알았어, 미안. 사실 나도 한때 동아리 선배 짝사랑했었잖아. 기억나?
lines.en: Okay, sorry. I mean, I once had a crush on a senior in my club too. Remember?

lines.ko: 아, 그 기타 치던 선배? 그때 너 맨날 동아리방에서 살았잖아.
lines.en: Oh, the senior who played guitar? You basically lived in the club room back then.

lines.ko: 응. 근데 결국 말도 못 하고 졸업했어. 차라리 그때 고백할 걸. 지금 생각하면 진짜 후회돼.
lines.en: Yeah. But I graduated without ever saying anything. I should've just confessed back then. Looking back, I really regret it.

lines.ko: 그 선배 지금 뭐 해?
lines.en: What's he up to now?

lines.ko: 결혼했어. 애도 둘이야.
lines.en: Married. Two kids.

lines.ko: 늦었네.
lines.en: Well, that ship has sailed.

lines.ko: 그니까 넌 나처럼 되지 마. 공연 끝나고 꼭 말해. 알았지?
lines.en: So don't end up like me. Tell her after the show, okay?

lines.ko: 알았어… 어? 잠깐만. 카톡 왔다.
lines.en: Okay… huh? Hang on. I got a message.

lines.ko: 누군데? 혹시?
lines.en: Who is it? Is it…?

lines.ko: …다은이.
lines.en: …Daeun.

lines.ko: 꺅, 뭐래, 뭐래? 보여 줘!
lines.en: What'd she say, what'd she say? Show me!

lines.ko: 야, 남의 카톡을 왜 봐. "현우야, 내일 연습 끝나고 뭐 해?"
lines.en: Hey, don't read other people's messages. "Hyunwoo, what are you doing after practice tomorrow?"

lines.ko: 대박. 이건 무조건 데이트 신청이야.
lines.en: No way. That's a hundred percent asking you out.

lines.ko: 아니야, 그냥 물어본 걸 수도 있지.
lines.en: Nah, she might just be asking.

lines.ko: 그냥 물어보는 사람이 밤 열한 시에 카톡을 해? 빨리 답장해.
lines.en: Who "just asks" at eleven at night? Reply, quick.

lines.ko: 너무 바로 하면 좀 없어 보이지 않을까? 한 십 분 있다가 할까?
lines.en: Won't I look desperate if I reply right away? Should I wait ten minutes or so?

lines.ko: 야, 요즘 누가 그런 걸 계산해. 그러다 다른 사람이 먼저 채 간다?
lines.en: Dude, who plays those games these days? Keep that up and someone else will snatch her first.

lines.ko: 아 알았어, 알았어. "아니, 아무것도 안 해. 왜?" …보냈다.
lines.en: Okay, okay. "Nope, nothing. Why?" …Sent.

lines.ko: 오, 읽었다! 답장 온다!
lines.en: Ooh, she read it! She's typing!

lines.ko: "그럼 우리 영화 보러 갈래? 새로 나온 공포 영화 있는데 너무 보고 싶어서!" …또 공포 영화야.
lines.en: "Then wanna go see a movie? There's a new horror movie out and I'm dying to see it!" …Horror again.

lines.ko: 너 어제 밤새운 보람 있네.
lines.en: Well, staying up all night paid off.

lines.ko: 웃지 마. 나 진짜 당황했어. 극장에서 소리라도 지르면 어떡해?
lines.en: Don't laugh. I'm seriously thrown. What if I scream in the cinema?

lines.ko: 그럼 차라리 솔직하게 말해. 사실 무서운 거 잘 못 본다고. 그런 모습 귀엽다고 할 수도 있잖아.
lines.en: Then just be honest. Tell her you're not great with scary stuff. She might think that's cute.

lines.ko: 그럴까? 아니야, 그냥 참고 볼래. 아니다, 솔직하게 말할까?
lines.en: Should I? No, I'll just tough it out. Wait, no, should I be honest?

lines.ko: 또, 또. 하나만 정해!
lines.en: There you go again. Pick one!

lines.ko: 알았어. 일단 "좋아!"라고 보낼게. 무서우면… 눈 감지, 뭐.
lines.en: Fine. I'll send "Sure!" for now. If it's scary… I'll just close my eyes.

lines.ko: 파이팅. 아, 너무 설렌다. 남의 연애인데 내가 더 떨려.
lines.en: Good luck. Oh, this is so exciting. It's your love life and I'm the one who's nervous.

lines.ko: 근데 넌? 소개팅 두 번 했다며. 어땠어?
lines.en: What about you? Heard you went on two blind dates. How were they?

lines.ko: 아, 몰라. 둘 다 도토리 키 재기야.
lines.en: Ugh, don't ask. Both equally meh.

lines.ko: 왜?
lines.en: Why?

lines.ko: 한 명은 두 시간 내내 자기 얘기만 하고, 한 명은 내가 무슨 말을 해도 리액션이 하나도 없어.
lines.en: One talked about himself for two hours straight, and the other didn't react to a single thing I said.

lines.ko: 넌 맞장구 잘 쳐 주는 사람 좋아하잖아.
lines.en: And you like people who play along.

lines.ko: 그니까. 아, 오늘은 네 얘기가 최고의 안줏거리다. 덕분에 팀장 생각 하나도 안 났어.
lines.en: Exactly. Ah, your story was the best thing to have with drinks tonight. Thanks to you, I didn't think about my team leader once.

lines.ko: 다행이네. 어? 근데 지금 몇 시야?
lines.en: Glad to hear it. Huh? Wait, what time is it?

lines.ko: 열한 시 오십 분… 헉, 막차!
lines.en: 11:50… Oh no, the last train!

lines.ko: 뛰어! 사장님, 여기 계산이요! 잘 먹었습니다!
lines.en: Run! Excuse me, can we pay? Thanks for the food!

lines.ko: 헉, 헉… 아, 방금 출발했어. 막차 끊겼다.
lines.en: Huff… ugh, it just left. We missed the last train.

lines.ko: 아… 차라리 아까 일어날 걸.
lines.en: Ugh… we should've just left earlier.

lines.ko: 됐어, 택시 타자. 아까 술값은 네가 냈으니까 택시비는 내가 낼게.
lines.en: Forget it, let's grab a taxi. You paid for the drinks, so I'll get the taxi.

lines.ko: 오케이. 대신 다은이 얘기는 진짜 비밀이다?
lines.en: Okay. But the Daeun thing stays a secret, got it?

lines.ko: 당연하지. 너도 민지 얘기 비밀이다?
lines.en: Obviously. And the Minji thing stays a secret too.

lines.ko: 알았어, 알았어.
lines.en: Yeah, yeah.

lines.ko: 아, 근데 다은이한테 "좋아"라고 보냈어?
lines.en: Oh, wait, did you actually send "Sure" to Daeun?

lines.ko: …아직.
lines.en: …Not yet.

lines.ko: 야! 지금 당장 보내!
lines.en: Hey! Send it right now!

lines.ko: 자, 이제 장면에서 잠깐 나와 볼게요. 안녕하세요, 수아예요!
lines.en: Okay, let's step out of the scene for a bit. Hi, I'm Sua!

lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 준이에요. 오늘은 친한 친구 둘이 금요일 밤에 포차에서 수다 떠는 장면이었어요.
lines.en: Hi, I'm Jun. Today's scene was two close friends chatting at a pojangmacha on a Friday night.

lines.ko: 대학 동기라서 처음부터 끝까지 반말이었죠.
lines.en: They went to university together, so it was casual speech from start to finish.

lines.ko: 맞아요. 대신 사장님한테는 해요체를 썼어요. "소주도 한 병 주세요!" 이렇게요.
lines.en: Right. But with the owner they used polite speech. Like, "And a bottle of soju, please!"

lines.ko: 첫 대화부터 재밌었어요. "너 왜 이렇게 일찍 왔어?" "늦을까 봐."
lines.en: The very first exchange was fun. "Why are you here so early?" "In case I was late."

lines.ko: 원래는 "늦을까 봐 걱정돼서 일찍 왔어"예요. 근데 친구끼리는 뒷부분 빼고 '-ㄹ까 봐'로 그냥 끝내요.
lines.en: The full version is "I was worried I'd be late, so I came early." But between friends you drop the rest and just end on "-ㄹ까 봐".

lines.ko: 아, 그럼 "왜 우산 가져왔어?" 하면 "비 올까 봐."
lines.en: Oh, so if someone asks "Why'd you bring an umbrella?", it's "In case it rains."

lines.ko: 그쵸, 딱 그거예요.
lines.en: Yep, exactly that.

lines.ko: 잠깐 멈추고 말해 보세요. 친구가 "왜 안 자?"라고 물어요. 내일 발표 망칠까 봐 걱정돼서 못 자는 거라면?
lines.en: Pause and try it. A friend asks, "Why aren't you asleep?" You can't sleep because you're worried you'll mess up tomorrow's presentation. What do you say?

lines.ko: "내일 발표 망칠까 봐."
lines.en: "In case I mess up tomorrow's presentation."

lines.ko: 팀장 얘기에서는 '-더니'가 나왔어요. "아침에 부장님한테 엄청 깨지더니, 자리 오자마자 나한테 화풀이하더라."
lines.en: In the team leader story, "-더니" came up. "He got chewed out by the department head this morning, and the second he got back to his desk he took it out on me."

lines.ko: '-더니'는 다른 사람이 뭘 하고, 그다음에 또 다른 걸 하는 걸 내가 봤을 때 써요.
lines.en: You use "-더니" when you saw someone else do one thing, and then something else after it.

lines.ko: 민지 얘기도 그랬죠? "화장실 간다고 하더니 몰래 집에 가 버렸어."
lines.en: Like the Minji story, right? "She said she was going to the bathroom and then snuck off home."

lines.ko: 맞아요. 근데 내 행동이랑 그 결과를 말할 때는 '-았/었더니'예요. "밥을 많이 먹었더니 졸려."
lines.en: Exactly. But when it's your own action and its result, it's "-았/었더니". "I ate a lot, and now I'm sleepy."

lines.ko: 지금 제 상태네요. 근데 '화풀이하다'는 '짜증 내다'랑 비슷해요?
lines.en: That's me right now. But is "화풀이하다" similar to "짜증 내다"?

lines.ko: 좀 달라요. '짜증 내다'는 그냥 신경질 내는 거고, '화풀이하다'는 다른 데서 난 화를 상관없는 사람한테 푸는 거예요. "왜 나한테 화풀이해?"
lines.en: A bit different. "짜증 내다" is just being cranky, but "화풀이하다" is taking anger from somewhere else out on someone who had nothing to do with it. "Why are you taking it out on me?"

lines.ko: 지수 씨 완전 억울했겠다. 그래서 "나 진짜 당황했어"라고 했구나.
lines.en: Poor Jisu, that's so unfair. That's why she said, "I was so thrown."

lines.ko: 네. '당황하다'는 갑자기 생긴 일 때문에 어쩔 줄 모르는 거예요. 상황이 말도 안 될 때는 '황당하다'고요.
lines.en: Yes. "당황하다" is not knowing what to do because something sudden happened. When a situation is just absurd, it's "황당하다".

lines.ko: '무시하다'도 뜻이 두 개죠?
lines.en: And "무시하다" has two meanings, right?

lines.ko: 네. "전화를 무시하다"는 못 본 척하는 거고, "사람을 무시하다"는 그 사람을 낮게 보는 거예요.
lines.en: Yes. "Ignoring a call" is pretending you didn't see it, and "looking down on someone" is treating them as beneath you.

lines.ko: 지수 씨 팀장은 둘 다네요.
lines.en: Jisu's team leader does both.

lines.ko: 그니까요. 게다가 이 팀장, "고집이 얼마나 센지, 한번 정하면 아무도 못 말려."
lines.en: Right? And on top of that, this guy is "so stubborn that once he's decided something, no one can stop him."

lines.ko: 아, '얼마나 -은지'!
lines.en: Oh, "얼마나 -은지"!

lines.ko: 네. 뒤에는 그래서 생긴 결과를 말해요. 형용사는 '-은지', 동사는 '-는지'. "그 집 김치찌개가 얼마나 맛있는지 맨날 줄 서야 돼."
lines.en: Yes. After it, you say the result. Adjectives take "-은지", verbs take "-는지". "That place's kimchi stew is so good you always have to queue."

lines.ko: 근데 '고집이 세다'의 '세다'는… 숫자 세는 '세다'예요?
lines.en: But the "세다" in "고집이 세다"… is that the counting "세다"?

lines.ko: 아뇨, 이건 강하다는 뜻이에요. 소리는 같은데 완전 달라요.
lines.en: No, this one means strong. Same sound, totally different word.

lines.ko: 그런 사람한테는 "얘기가 안 통해"라고 하죠.
lines.en: And with someone like that, you say "You can't get through to him."

lines.ko: 맞아요. 반대로 대화가 잘 되면 "말이 잘 통해."
lines.en: Right. And the opposite, when you click, is "We really get each other."

lines.ko: 현우 씨는 "완전 전형적인 꼰대네"라고 했어요.
lines.en: Hyunwoo said, "Classic old-school jerk boss."

lines.ko: '전형적이다'는 딱 그런 종류의 대표 같다는 말이에요. 좀 부정적으로 많이 써요. "전형적인 월요일이네."
lines.en: "전형적이다" means it's a textbook example of that type. It's often used a bit negatively. "Such a typical Monday."

lines.ko: 그리고 지수 씨가 "모르는 소리 좀 하지 마"라고 했는데, 좀 세게 들려요.
lines.en: And Jisu said, "You don't know what you're talking about." That sounds kind of harsh.

lines.ko: 네, 아주 친한 친구한테만 써요. "잘 모르면서 말하지 마"라는 뜻이에요.
lines.en: Yes, only with really close friends. It means "Don't talk when you don't know the situation."

lines.ko: 비슷하게 "무슨 소리야"도 있죠?
lines.en: And there's "무슨 소리야" too, right?

lines.ko: 네, "그게 무슨 말이야?" 하는 거예요. 근데 고마워할 때도 써요. "무슨 소리야, 당연히 도와줘야지." 존댓말로는 "무슨 소리예요?"
lines.en: Yes, it's like "What do you mean?" But you also use it when someone thanks you. "What are you talking about, of course I'll help." Politely, it's "무슨 소리예요?"

lines.ko: "아… 그래서 너 요즘 연락이 없었구나."
lines.en: "Ah… so that's why I haven't heard from you lately."

lines.ko: '그래서 -았/었구나'는 이유를 알고 나서 "아, 그래서 그랬구나" 할 때 써요.
lines.en: "그래서 -았/었구나" is for when you find out the reason and go, "Ah, so that's why."

lines.ko: 윗사람한테도 '-구나' 써도 돼요?
lines.en: Can you use "-구나" with someone senior too?

lines.ko: 그건 안 돼요. "아, 그래서 연락이 없으셨군요"나 "그래서 그러셨네요"라고 해야 돼요.
lines.en: No, you can't. You'd say "Ah, so that's why I hadn't heard from you" with "-셨군요", or "So that's why, then" with "-셨네요".

lines.ko: 잠깐 멈추고 말해 보세요. 친구가 어제 감기에 걸렸대요. 그래서 학교에 안 온 거예요. 반말로?
lines.en: Pause and say it. Your friend says they caught a cold yesterday. That's why they didn't come to school. In casual speech?

lines.ko: "아, 그래서 어제 안 왔구나."
lines.en: "Ah, so that's why you didn't come yesterday."

lines.ko: 민지 얘기도 했죠. "헐, 진짜 얌체 같다."
lines.en: They talked about Minji too. "Wow, what a freeloader."

lines.ko: '얌체'는 자기 이익만 챙기는 사람이에요. 계산할 때만 사라지거나, 줄 새치기하는 사람.
lines.en: An "얌체" is someone who only looks out for themselves. The person who vanishes when the bill comes, or cuts the queue.

lines.ko: 다들 한 명씩은 알죠. '몰래'는요?
lines.en: Everyone knows one. What about "몰래"?

lines.ko: 다른 사람이 모르게, 라는 뜻이에요. "엄마 몰래 게임했어." 이렇게요.
lines.en: It means without the other person knowing. Like, "I played games behind my mum's back."

lines.ko: '비밀'은 어떤 말이랑 같이 써요?
lines.en: What words go with "비밀"?

lines.ko: '비밀을 지키다', '비밀을 털어놓다'. 이게 제일 많이 나와요.
lines.en: "To keep a secret" and "to spill a secret". Those come up the most.

lines.ko: 근데 '욕하다'는 욕설만 말하는 거 아니에요?
lines.en: But doesn't "욕하다" just mean swearing?

lines.ko: 아니에요. 나쁜 말을 하는 것도 '욕하다', 다른 사람 흉을 보는 것도 '욕하다'예요. "내 욕하고 다닌대."
lines.en: Nope. Swearing is "욕하다", and badmouthing someone is "욕하다" too. "Apparently she's been badmouthing me."

lines.ko: 뒤에서 하는 욕은 '뒷담화'!
lines.en: And badmouthing behind someone's back is "뒷담화"!

lines.ko: 맞아요. 그리고 지수 씨가 "넌 맞장구를 진짜 잘 쳐 줘서 얘기할 맛이 난다"라고 했죠.
lines.en: Right. And Jisu said, "You're so good at backing me up, it actually makes me want to talk."

lines.ko: "그치?", "내 말이!", "헐" 이런 거요?
lines.en: Like "Right?", "Exactly!", "No way"?

lines.ko: 네, 상대방 말에 맞춰서 반응해 주는 걸 '맞장구를 치다'라고 해요.
lines.en: Yes, reacting along with what the other person says is "맞장구를 치다".

lines.ko: 이제 연애 얘기! "너네 요즘 맨날 같이 다니던데." "난 너네 사귀는 줄 알았어."
lines.en: Now the love story! "You two are always together these days." "I thought you two were dating."

lines.ko: '같이 다니다'는 어디든 함께 가는 거예요. 그리고 '-은/는 줄 알았어요', 이거 진짜 중요해요.
lines.en: "같이 다니다" means going everywhere together. And "-은/는 줄 알았어요" is really important.

lines.ko: 왜요?
lines.en: Why?

lines.ko: 그렇게 생각했는데 사실은 아니었다는 뜻이거든요. "사귀는 줄 알았어"는 안 사귀는 거예요.
lines.en: Because it means you thought so, but it wasn't true. "I thought they were dating" means they're not.

lines.ko: 그럼 "사귀는 줄 몰랐어"는요?
lines.en: Then what about "I didn't know they were dating"?

lines.ko: 그건 사귀는 거죠.
lines.en: That means they are.

lines.ko: 와, 완전 반대네요. 그다음엔 "아니긴 뭐가 아니야. 귀까지 빨간데."
lines.en: Wow, total opposites. And after that: "What do you mean, no? Even your ears are red."

lines.ko: 상대방은 아니라는데, 내가 보기엔 확실히 맞을 때 써요. "괜찮긴 뭐가 괜찮아, 얼굴이 하얀데."
lines.en: You use it when the other person says no, but you can clearly see it's yes. "What do you mean you're fine? You're white as a sheet."

lines.ko: 이것도 반말이죠?
lines.en: That's casual speech too, right?

lines.ko: 네, 가족이나 아주 친한 친구한테만 써요.
lines.en: Yes, only with family or really close friends.

lines.ko: 잠깐 멈추고 말해 보세요. 친구가 하나도 안 피곤하대요. 근데 눈이 반쯤 감겼어요. 그러면?
lines.en: Pause and say it. Your friend says they're not tired at all. But their eyes are half closed. What do you say?

lines.ko: "안 피곤하긴 뭐가 안 피곤해. 눈이 반쯤 감겼는데."
lines.en: "What do you mean, not tired? Your eyes are half shut."

lines.ko: 그리고 "너 진짜 다은이 좋아하는구나!"
lines.en: And "So you really do like Daeun!"

lines.ko: '-구나'는 새로 알게 된 걸 말하는 반말이에요. 동사는 '-는구나', 형용사는 '-구나'. "오늘 춥구나."
lines.en: "-구나" is casual speech for something you've just realised. Verbs take "-는구나", adjectives take "-구나". "Oh, it's cold today."

lines.ko: 혼잣말로도 많이 쓰죠?
lines.en: People use it a lot when talking to themselves too, right?

lines.ko: 네, 엄청 많이 써요.
lines.en: Yes, all the time.

lines.ko: 다은 씨 목소리가 독특하다고 했잖아요. '특이하다'랑 같아요?
lines.en: He said Daeun's voice is "독특하다". Is that the same as "특이하다"?

lines.ko: '특이하다'는 좀 이상하다는 느낌도 있는데, '독특하다'는 대부분 칭찬이에요.
lines.en: "특이하다" can feel a bit like "weird", but "독특하다" is mostly a compliment.

lines.ko: 그리고 "그 뒤로 자꾸 생각나." '자꾸'는 '계속'이랑 똑같아요?
lines.en: And "Ever since, I keep thinking about her." Is "자꾸" exactly the same as "계속"?

lines.ko: 비슷한데, '자꾸'는 내 마음대로 안 되고 또 또 그런다는 느낌이에요.
lines.en: Similar, but "자꾸" has the feeling that it keeps happening again and again, whether you like it or not.

lines.ko: 아, 그래서 짝사랑할 때 딱이네요.
lines.en: Oh, so it's perfect for a crush.

lines.ko: 그쵸. 아, 그리고 '여배우'는 요즘은 그냥 '배우'라고 더 많이 해요.
lines.en: Exactly. Oh, and for "actress", these days people mostly just say "배우".

lines.ko: "다은이가 내 어깨를 툭 치더니"! 그리고 "아직도 웃음이 나."
lines.en: "She gave my shoulder a little tap"! And "I still can't help grinning."

lines.ko: '툭'은 가볍게 치는 소리예요. '웃음이 나다'는 웃으려고 한 게 아닌데 저절로 웃음이 나오는 거고요. '화가 나다'처럼요.
lines.en: "툭" is the sound of a light tap. "웃음이 나다" is when a laugh just comes out without you trying. Like "화가 나다".

lines.ko: "이런저런 얘기"는 이것저것 여러 가지 얘기죠?
lines.en: And "이런저런 얘기" is talking about this and that, right?

lines.ko: 맞아요.
lines.en: That's right.

lines.ko: 고백한다고 했다가 안 한다고 했다가… "왜 이랬다 저랬다 해?"
lines.en: He'll confess, then he won't… "Why do you keep changing your mind?"

lines.ko: 마음을 자꾸 바꾸는 사람한테 써요. 같은 모양으로 "왔다 갔다 하다", "불을 껐다 켰다 하다"도 있어요.
lines.en: You say it to someone who keeps changing their mind. The same shape shows up in "to go back and forth" and "to keep switching the light off and on".

lines.ko: '차라리'는 두 번 나왔어요. "차라리 빨리 말해." 그리고 "차라리 그때 고백할 걸."
lines.en: "차라리" came up twice. "You might as well tell her soon." And "I should've just confessed back then."

lines.ko: '차라리'는 둘 다 별로일 때 덜 나쁜 쪽을 고르는 말이에요.
lines.en: "차라리" is for picking the less bad option when neither is great.

lines.ko: 그럼 '차라리 -ㄹ 걸'은요?
lines.en: And "차라리 -ㄹ 걸"?

lines.ko: 그렇게 안 한 걸 후회할 때 써요. "이렇게 막힐 거면 차라리 지하철 탈 걸."
lines.en: That's for regretting not doing something. "If traffic was going to be this bad, I should've just taken the subway."

lines.ko: 잠깐 멈추고 말해 보세요. 택시가 너무 막혀요. 걸어갈 걸 후회하면?
lines.en: Pause and say it. Your taxi is stuck in traffic. You wish you'd walked. What do you say?

lines.ko: "차라리 걸어갈 걸."
lines.en: "I should've just walked."

lines.ko: 공포 영화 얘기! "다은이가 공포 영화를 엄청 좋아한다는데."
lines.en: The horror movie part! "Apparently Daeun loves horror movies."

lines.ko: '-다는데'는 들은 얘기를 먼저 하고, 그다음에 내 행동이나 제안을 말할 때 써요. "토요일에 불꽃 축제 한다는데, 같이 갈래?"
lines.en: "-다는데" is for saying what you heard first, then what you'll do or suggest. "I hear there's a fireworks festival on Saturday, wanna go?"

lines.ko: 그래서 현우 씨는 밤새웠고요.
lines.en: And so Hyunwoo stayed up all night.

lines.ko: 네, '밤새우다'는 잠 안 자고 밤을 보내는 거예요. 근데 현우 씨가 "내가 밤새 만든 자료"라고도 했죠?
lines.en: Yes, "밤새우다" is spending the night without sleeping. But Hyunwoo also said "the material I stayed up all night making", right?

lines.ko: 아, 그 '밤새'는 달라요?
lines.en: Oh, is that "밤새" different?

lines.ko: 그건 '밤 동안'이라는 뜻이라서 조금 달라요.
lines.en: That one means "through the night", so it's a little different.

lines.ko: 친구가 그런 짓을 하면 "제정신이니?"
lines.en: And if a friend does something like that: "Are you out of your mind?"

lines.ko: 네, 좀 센 말이라서 친한 사이에서만 써요.
lines.en: Yes, it's pretty strong, so only between close friends.

lines.ko: '잔인하다'랑 '오싹하다'는요?
lines.en: What about "잔인하다" and "오싹하다"?

lines.ko: 피가 많이 나오면 '잔인하다', 등에 찬 바람이 쓱 지나가는 느낌이면 '오싹하다'예요.
lines.en: If there's a lot of blood, it's "잔인하다". If it feels like a cold draft just ran down your back, it's "오싹하다".

lines.ko: 그리고 짝사랑 얘기가 너무 공감됐다고 했죠.
lines.en: And he said the crush story was so relatable.

lines.ko: '공감되다'는 노래나 이야기가 꼭 내 얘기 같을 때 써요. "이 노래 가사 너무 공감돼."
lines.en: "공감되다" is when a song or story feels just like your own life. "These lyrics are so relatable."

lines.ko: 지수 씨는 "사실 나도 한때 동아리 선배 짝사랑했었잖아"라고 했어요.
lines.en: Jisu said, "I mean, I once had a crush on a senior in my club too."

lines.ko: '한때'는 지나간 어느 시기예요. 그리고 소개팅 상대 둘은 "도토리 키 재기"였죠.
lines.en: "한때" is some time in the past. And her two blind dates were "도토리 키 재기".

lines.ko: 도토리끼리 키를 재 봤자…
lines.en: Acorns comparing heights…

lines.ko: 다 비슷하잖아요. 둘 다 거기서 거기라는 말이에요.
lines.en: They're all the same size. It means neither is any better than the other.

lines.ko: 마지막엔 "네 얘기가 최고의 안줏거리다." 그리고 "헉, 막차!"
lines.en: At the end: "Your story was the best thing to have with drinks tonight." And "Oh no, the last train!"

lines.ko: '안줏거리'는 원래 술이랑 먹는 음식인데, 술 마시면서 할 재밌는 이야기라는 뜻도 있어요.
lines.en: "안줏거리" is originally food to go with drinks, but it also means a juicy story to talk about over drinks.

lines.ko: 오늘은 현우 씨 연애가 안줏거리였네요.
lines.en: So tonight Hyunwoo's love life was the snack.

lines.ko: 그쵸. '막차'는 마지막 지하철이나 버스예요. 반대는 '첫차'. 막차가 이미 갔으면 "막차 끊겼어."
lines.en: Pretty much. "막차" is the last subway or bus. The opposite is "첫차". If it's already gone, you say "The last train's gone."

lines.ko: 자, 마지막으로 빠르게 복습해 볼게요. 제가 상황을 말하면 바로 반말로 말해 보세요.
lines.en: Okay, let's do a quick review to finish. I'll give you a situation, and you answer straight away in casual speech.

lines.ko: 친구가 왜 일찍 왔냐고 물어요. 늦을까 봐 걱정돼서요.
lines.en: A friend asks why you came early. You were worried you'd be late.

lines.ko: "늦을까 봐."
lines.en: "In case I was late."

lines.ko: 팀장이 부장님한테 혼나고 나서 나한테 화를 냈어요.
lines.en: Your team leader got told off by the department head, then got angry at you.

lines.ko: "부장님한테 깨지더니 나한테 화풀이하더라."
lines.en: "He got chewed out by the department head, then took it out on me."

lines.ko: 둘이 사귀는 거라고 생각했는데 아니었어요.
lines.en: You thought those two were dating, but they weren't.

lines.ko: "난 너네 사귀는 줄 알았어."
lines.en: "I thought you two were dating."

lines.ko: 친구가 아니라는데 얼굴이 빨개요.
lines.en: Your friend says no, but their face is red.

lines.ko: "아니긴 뭐가 아니야."
lines.en: "What do you mean, no?"

lines.ko: 친구가 자꾸 마음을 바꿔요.
lines.en: Your friend keeps changing their mind.

lines.ko: "왜 이랬다 저랬다 해?"
lines.en: "Why do you keep changing your mind?"

lines.ko: 그때 고백 안 한 게 후회돼요.
lines.en: You regret not confessing back then.

lines.ko: "차라리 그때 고백할 걸."
lines.en: "I should've just confessed back then."

lines.ko: 친구가 새벽 세 시에 혼자 등산 간대요.
lines.en: Your friend says they're going hiking alone at 3 a.m.

lines.ko: "제정신이니?"
lines.en: "Are you out of your mind?"

lines.ko: 둘 다 별로고 비슷비슷해요.
lines.en: Both options are meh and pretty much the same.

lines.ko: "완전 도토리 키 재기야."
lines.en: "Six of one, half a dozen of the other."

lines.ko: 좋아요! 오늘도 수고 많으셨어요. 다음 회에서 또 만나요!
lines.en: Great! Thanks for all your hard work today. See you next episode!

lines.ko: 안녕히 계세요!
lines.en: Bye!
